title: Pregnancy
description: How a pregnancy begins, is known, is chosen, may be lost and ends in birth (M2.6 step 4, D96, D97), and a child's care after (step 4b, D98). The figures trace to CALIBRATION.md.

night.description: The chance in ten thousand that a night together begins a pregnancy: without protection, and with a condom used as most people use one.

ages.description: The carrier's age and the share of the chance left at it, per hundred: the last band at or under their age counts.

known.description: The week a pregnancy is known: a missed period, then a test.

loss.description: Miscarriage: per thousand known pregnancies, and the share of those in the first trimester, per hundred.

end.description: Ending a pregnancy at a clinic, on a weekday in its hours: by pills up to a week, by a procedure after, until the legal limit (D97).

pills.description: The last week pills are given.

limit.description: The last week it can be ended.

partner.description: The chance in a hundred a partner who carries goes on with the pregnancy: their choice, not yours (tune).

term.description: Birth: the week it can come from, and the days after over which it falls.

birth.description: Cents a birth costs the one who gives birth.

care.description: A child living with you (D98): minutes of care a day by age, what a partner you live with takes on, daycare while you work, and what follows care not given.

needs.description: Minutes of care a day for a child under each age in years: the first band they're under counts.

partner.description: Per hundred of the care a partner you live with gives.

sitting.description: Minutes of care a sitting of it is, at most.

daycare.description: Paid care while you work, for a child under the age.

neglect.description: Days without enough care, within a window of days, that bring a report to child protective services.

investigation.description: Days an investigation takes once a report is made.

support.description: Custody and child support when parents part (step 4c, D100), by the shape of Michigan's formula: each parent's share of the base support from their share of the income, offset by the nights each has the child.

hours.description: Hours a week a working parent is taken to work.

keep.description: Per hundred of gross pay kept after tax.

base.description: Per hundred of the parents' combined net income, the base support for one child, two, and so on.

nights.description: Nights a year with each parent under the standard parenting time.
